title: [28/1/2023] Percentage of time working adults spent on different activities
prompt: The chart below shows the percentage of the day working adults spent doing different activities in a particular country in 1958 and in 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts compare how working adults in a particular country spent their time on various daily activities in 1958 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the proportions of time spent on working, commuting and relaxing at home increased over the 50-year period, there were significant decreases in sleeping and going out hours, with other activities remaining unchanged. In addition, working hours consistently took up the largest share of the day.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the two most time-consuming activities, working and sleeping took up similar proportions of the day in 1958, at 33% and 32% respectively. Over the next five decades, working hours increased significantly, accounting for 42% of people's daily time. In contrast, time spent sleeping decreased to one-quarter of the day by 2008.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining activities, going out with friends and family occupied 19% of the day in 1958, while relaxing at home and other activities took up much smaller proportions at 8% and 6% respectively, and only 2% was spent on travelling to work. By 2008, there was a dramatic fall in socializing time to just 6%, while both relaxing at home and commuting saw increases to 13% and 8% respectively. Meanwhile, the proportion of time dedicated to other activities remained stable at 6% throughout the period.
